     3→> Atomic development workflow for building Bivvy.
     4→
     5→<steps>
     6→  <step number="1" id="specification">
     7→    <title>Specification</title>
     8→    <goal>Define the contract your code must fulfill before writing implementation.</goal>
     9→    <instructions>
    10→      <instruction>
    11→        Define the Behavior: Create test files first. Tests are the specification.
    12→        <conditional>
    13→          <condition>Test files already exist</condition>
    14→          <action>Update tests to match the new/changed behavior</action>
    15→        </conditional>
    16→      </instruction>
    17→      <instruction>
    18→        <command>cargo test --all-features</command>
    19→        <expected>All new or updated tests should FAIL</expected>
    20→        <rationale>Failing tests prove they're actually testing new logic, not passing by accident.</rationale>
    21→      </instruction>
    22→    </instructions>
    23→    <gate>
    24→      <condition>New tests fail for the right reasons</condition>
    25→      <on_fail>Refine your tests until they correctly specify the behavior</on_fail>
    26→    </gate>
    27→  </step>
    28→
    29→  <step number="2" id="implementation">
    30→    <title>Implementation</title>
    31→    <goal>Write the minimum code to make tests pass.</goal>
    32→    <prerequisite ref="specification">Failing tests from specification step</prerequisite>
    33→    <instructions>
    34→      <instruction>
    35→        Write the Code: Implement only what's needed to pass the tests. Resist adding "nice to have" features.
    36→      </instruction>
    37→      <instruction>
    38→        Keep it Simple: If you're writing more code than tests require, stop and reconsider.
    39→      </instruction>
    40→    </instructions>
    41→    <gate>
    42→      <condition>All tests pass</condition>
    43→      <on_fail>Continue implementing or fix bugs until green</on_fail>
    44→    </gate>
    45→  </step>
    46→
    47→  <step number="3" id="documentation">
    48→    <title>Documentation</title>
    49→    <goal>Document while context is fresh. User-facing and dev-facing docs are separate concerns.</goal>
    50→    <prerequisite ref="implementation">Tests passing</prerequisite>
    51→    <instructions>
    52→      <instruction>
    53→        Rustdoc Comments: Add `///` doc comments to all public items (structs, functions, modules). This is the primary form of API documentation.
    54→      </instruction>
    55→      <instruction>
    56→        User-Facing Docs: Update `docs/` if adding commands, config options, or user-visible features. These are Starlight pages written for end users — never reference internals.
    57→      </instruction>
    58→      <instruction>
    59→        Source READMEs: Update or create `README.md` in source directories (e.g., `src/cli/README.md`) when adding or changing subsystem design, architecture, or guiding principles.
    60→      </instruction>
    61→      <instruction>
    62→        Inline Comments: Add comments only where the "why" isn't obvious from the code.
    63→      </instruction>
    64→      <instruction>
    65→        Verify Docs Build: Confirm documentation compiles without errors.
    66→        <command>cargo doc --no-deps --all-features</command>
    67→        <expected>No documentation errors</expected>
    68→      </instruction>
    69→    </instructions>
    70→    <boundaries>
    71→      <rule>Developer docs go in source tree (rustdoc + source READMEs), never in `docs/`</rule>
    72→      <rule>User-facing docs go in `docs/`, never in source READMEs</rule>
    73→    </boundaries>
    74→    <anti-patterns>
    75→      <anti-pattern>Documenting "what" the code does (the code should show that)</anti-pattern>
    76→      <anti-pattern>Leaving documentation for later (it won't happen)</anti-pattern>
    77→      <anti-pattern>Over-commenting obvious code</anti-pattern>
    78→      <anti-pattern>Putting developer architecture docs in `docs/`</anti-pattern>
    79→      <anti-pattern>Putting user-facing guides in source READMEs</anti-pattern>
    80→    </anti-patterns>
    81→  </step>
    82→
    83→  <step number="4" id="linting">
    84→    <title>Static Quality Gate (Linting)</title>
    85→    <goal>Catch issues before they become problems.</goal>
    86→    <prerequisite ref="documentation">Implementation and documentation complete</prerequisite>
    87→    <instructions>
    88→      <instruction>
    89→        <command>cargo fmt -- --check</command>
    90→        <expected>No formatting differences</expected>
    91→        <fix>cargo fmt</fix>
    92→      </instruction>
    93→      <instruction>
    94→        <command>cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings</command>
    95→        <expected>No warnings or errors</expected>
    96→        <rationale>Warnings today become bugs tomorrow. Zero tolerance. Flags match CI.</rationale>
    97→      </instruction>
    98→    </instructions>
    99→    <gate>

   103→  </step>

   138→    <goal>Confirm production readiness.</goal>
   139→    <prerequisite ref="testing">All tests passing</prerequisite>

   163→      <instruction>

   208→    </instructions>
   209→  </step>

   213→    <goal>Clean context switch to next task.</goal>

   218→      <instruction goto="specification">

   220→      </instruction>
   221→    </instructions>
   222→  </step>

     5→## Project Overview

    22→  <step ref="documentation">Document while context is fresh (rustdoc for APIs, `docs/` for user-facing changes, source READMEs for design)</step>

    24→  <step ref="testing">Pass all tests with >90% coverage</step>

    48→  Every verification must run the ENTIRE test suite with all features.

     6→> Cross-language development environment setup automation, built in Rust.
     7→
     8→Bivvy replaces ad-hoc `bin/setup` scripts with declarative YAML configuration, smart state tracking, and a polished CLI.
     9→
    10→## Installation
    11→
    12→Quick install (macOS/Linux):

    59→## What It Does
    60→
    61→```yaml
    62→# .bivvy/config.yml
    63→app_name: myapp
    64→
    65→steps:
    66→  brew:
    67→    template: brew
    68→  ruby:
    69→    template: bundler
    70→    watches: [Gemfile.lock]
    71→  node:
    72→    template: yarn
    73→    watches: [yarn.lock]
    74→  db:
    75→    command: "rails db:prepare"
    76→    depends_on: [ruby]
    77→
    78→workflows:
    79→  default:
    80→    steps: [brew, ruby, node, db]
    81→```

    83→- **State tracking** — only re-runs what's needed

    87→- **Remote sources** — central team templates via HTTP or Git

Design an implementation plan for adding TOML configuration support to Bivvy, allowing users to use `.bivvy/config.toml` instead of `.bivvy/config.yml`.

## Current Architecture

The config loading is centralized in `src/config/loader.rs`. Key functions:

   - `find_project_config(root)` → `.bivvy/config.yml`
   - `find_project_local(root)` → `.bivvy/config.local.yml`

2. **`load_config_value(path)`** - Reads a file and parses it as `serde_yaml::Value`

3. **`load_config_file(path)`** - Reads a file, calls `parse_config()` which uses `serde_yaml::from_str()`

4. **`load_merged_config(project_root)`** - Discovers files, loads them all as `serde_yaml::Value`, deep merges via `merge_configs()`, then deserializes merged value with `serde_yaml::from_value()`

5. **`load_config(project_root, config_override)`** - Entry point; if override path given, loads single file; otherwise merges

The merge pipeline works on `serde_yaml::Value` (which is basically a generic JSON-like value tree). The merger in `merger.rs` operates on `serde_yaml::Value`.

## Config structs
All config structs derive `Serialize, Deserialize` via serde - they're format-agnostic.

## Other touchpoints
- `src/cli/commands/init.rs` - Creates `.bivvy/config.yml`, references the filename in messages
- `src/cli/args.rs` - CLI arg `--config` overrides default config path
- `src/config/mod.rs` - Module docs reference `.bivvy/config.yml`
- `src/lint/` - Various references to `config.yml` in test fixtures and diagnostics

## Requirements
- Add `toml` crate to Cargo.toml
- In `ConfigPaths::discover()`, check for both `.yml` and `.toml` variants (prefer TOML if both exist? Or error if both exist?)
- In `load_config_value()` and `load_config_file()`, detect format by extension and parse accordingly
- The merge pipeline currently uses `serde_yaml::Value`. For TOML files, we need to convert `toml::Value` to `serde_yaml::Value` (or use `serde_json::Value` as a common intermediate). Actually, since the structs are serde-compatible, we could: parse TOML → deserialize to `BivvyConfig` directly, or parse TOML → convert to `serde_yaml::Value` for merge compatibility.
- Need to handle the case where project uses config.toml but local override uses config.local.yml (or vice versa) — probably best to keep them consistent or support mixing.

## Design considerations
1. **Common value type for merging**: The merger operates on `serde_yaml::Value`. Options:
   a. Convert TOML values to `serde_yaml::Value` via serde (serialize toml::Value → deserialize as serde_yaml::Value using serde_json::Value as intermediate)
   b. Use `serde_json::Value` as the common merge type instead (would require refactoring merger.rs)
   c. Deserialize TOML content to `serde_yaml::Value` directly by going through JSON string
   
   Option (a) via `serde_json::Value` as bridge is cleanest: parse toml string → `toml::Value` → serialize to JSON → deserialize as `serde_yaml::Value`.

2. **File discovery**: When both `.yml` and `.toml` exist, should we error or pick one? Erroring is safest to avoid confusion.

3. **Init command**: Should `bivvy init` ask which format? Or always default to YAML for backwards compatibility?

4. **Config override path**: `load_config_file()` already takes a path, so it just needs to detect the extension.

Please produce a detailed, step-by-step implementation plan.

The merge pipeline works on `serde_yaml::Value` (which is basically a generic JSON-like value tree). The merger in `merger.rs` operates on `serde_yaml::Value`.

# Plan: TOML Configuration Support

## Context

Users want to write Bivvy configuration in TOML instead of YAML. The config structs already use format-agnostic serde derives, so the main work is in the loading layer: detecting the format, parsing TOML, converting to `serde_yaml::Value` for the existing merge pipeline, and handling dual-format file discovery.

## Approach

Add `toml` crate. Detect format by file extension. Convert TOML values to `serde_yaml::Value` via `serde_json::Value` bridge for merge compatibility. Error if both `.yml` and `.toml` exist for the same config slot.

## Files to Modify

1. **`Cargo.toml`** — Add `toml = "0.8"` dependency
2. **`src/config/loader.rs`** — Core changes:
   - Add `ConfigFormat` enum with `from_path()` detection
   - Add `toml_str_to_yaml_value()` conversion helper
   - Update `load_config_value()` to detect format and parse accordingly
   - Update `parse_config()` to support both formats
   - Update `ConfigPaths` finder methods to check `.toml` and `.yml`
   - Add `ConfigPaths::validate_no_format_conflicts()`
   - Call conflict validation in `load_merged_config_with_resolver()`
   - Add tests for all new functionality
3. **`src/config/mod.rs`** — Export `ConfigFormat`
4. **`src/config/extends.rs`** — Detect TOML format from URL extension in extends resolver
5. **`src/cli/commands/init.rs`** — Update `config_exists()` to check both formats; update gitignore to cover `.toml` local override
6. **`src/cli/args.rs`** — Add `--format` flag to init args (yaml/toml, default yaml)

## Key Design Decisions

- **Format detection**: By file extension (`.yml`/`.yaml` = YAML, `.toml` = TOML)
- **Conflict handling**: Error if both formats exist for same config slot (e.g., both `config.yml` and `config.toml`)
- **Mixed layers OK**: Project can use `config.toml` while global uses `config.yml`
- **Merge compatibility**: TOML parsed → `serde_json::Value` → `serde_yaml::Value`, keeping merger.rs untouched
- **Init default**: Still YAML unless `--format toml` is passed
- **TOML null limitation**: TOML has no null type, so null-deletion in merging won't work from TOML files (acceptable, document it)

## Verification

```bash
cargo test --all-features
cargo fmt -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo build --release
```
